paragraphs: Paul tells the Galatians that the blessing of Abraham reaches the nations “that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.” The psalmist sings that the Lord “will ever be mindful of his covenant.” In the Gospel, when a demon is cast out by “the finger of God,” the crowd prefers to invent an explanation rather than accept the sign. The thread through all three is that God keeps his promise by giving his Spirit, and the Spirit is received by trust, never by cleverness or possession.
Augustine, preaching on the same exorcism as Matthew tells it, says what the Spirit does:

quote.text: For by the Holy Spirit, by whom the people of God are gathered together into one, is the unclean spirit who is divided against himself cast out.
quote.attribution: St Augustine, Sermon 21 on the New Testament Lessons (Ben. 71), on Matthew 12, the parallel to Luke 11:15–26, §19
quote.translation: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 6 (ed. P. Schaff)

closing: Then Jesus adds a warning meant to steady us: a house swept clean but left empty invites worse tenants. It is not enough to be rid of a sin; the heart must be occupied by the One promised to Abraham. So ask today not only what you must expel, but whom you are welcoming. Let one act of trust, a prayer or a reconciliation, fill the space. The Lord remembers his covenant; remember it with him.
